item.title: Same Nickname, Two Very Different Men—Part One
item.description: AUTHOR’S NOTE: A few times each year, someone who knows of my enjoyment of historical research contacts me to see whether I can solve a mystery. Whatever happened to so-and-so? Does such-and-such a business still exist? Who named that lake or that creek? Who was the first to do this or that? And on and on. Sometimes the answers to such questions are relatively easy to find; other times I can find nothing at all.

item.title: Almond joy popped quinoa granola adds a taste of whimsy
item.description: I once marveled at turning 10. I remember looking back at the experiences of my life thus far and feeling that I had lived a long life already, and I was correct, in a way. At just 10 years old I had indeed experienced more than many of my peers and had learned things about the world that perhaps I shouldn’t have so young. I felt wise, but of course I was not, and would not learn that truth for many years. I saw my future self clearly then — professional, refined, accomplished, successful, and worldly. I had no doubts that I would get there — all I had to do was be a good student and get a college degree, and my life would be whatever I wanted it to be.
